security_spec.violation_condition: In the KVM hypervisor (arch/riscv/kvm), when henvcfg.PMM is changed for a guest with hgatp.MODE in {sv48x4, sv57x4} and vsatp.MODE=Bare, without a subsequent HFENCE.GVMA with rs1=x0, stale TLB entries may alias guest-physical addresses differing only in the top 2 masked bits to the same supervisor-physical page.
security_spec.summary: KVM must issue HFENCE.GVMA(rs1=x0) on henvcfg.PMM changes when hgatp uses x4 modes and vsatp.MODE=Bare, else GPA masking causes TLB-alias data corruption across guest pages

findings.finding: When guest changes henvcfg.PMM via SBI FWFT SET (non-one_reg_access path), csr_write(CSR_HENVCFG, ...) directly modifies hardware without a subsequent HFENCE.GVMA. If vsatp.MODE=Bare and hgatp.MODE is sv48x4 or sv57x4, stale G-stage TLB entries may alias guest-physical addresses differing only in the top masked bits to the same supervisor-physical page, causing data corruption. The RISC-V privileged spec requires TLB invalidation after changing translation-relevant CSRs.

VCPU reset sets csr->vsatp = 0 (Bare mode). Combined with the PMM-change-via-SBI path above, a freshly reset guest that enables pointer masking while still in Bare mode (before setting up VS-stage paging) satisfies all conditions for the stale-TLB vulnerability: vsatp.MODE=Bare, hgatp.MODE in {sv48x4,sv57x4}, and no HFENCE.GVMA after PMM change.

This function correctly swaps scounteren, senvcfg, and sstateen0 between host and guest. henvcfg is not handled here, which is correct since henvcfg is an HS-mode CSR written during kvm_arch_vcpu_load() and does not need per-guest-entry swap. senvcfg (the S-mode envcfg visible to the guest) is properly swapped via csr_swap at line 756.
findings.snippet:
vcpu->arch.host_scounteren = csr_swap(CSR_SCOUNTEREN, csr->scounteren);
vcpu->arch.host_senvcfg = csr_swap(CSR_SENVCFG, csr->senvcfg);

findings.finding: hgatp update is correctly followed by HFENCE.GVMA when no hardware VMID support exists (line 614-615). When hardware VMID is available, the sanitize path in kvm_riscv_local_tlb_sanitize() handles CPU migration. This function does not contribute to the vulnerability.

TLB sanitize correctly handles CPU migration by flushing G-stage TLB when the host CPU changes. However, it returns early when last_exit_cpu == cpu (line 166), meaning it cannot catch the in-place PMM change that occurs during a single vCPU run on the same CPU. This is by design — the sanitize is for cross-CPU migration, not for CSR changes mid-execution.

During initialization, try_to_set_pmm() directly sets and clears PMM on the hardware CSR to probe PMLEN support. The csr_read_clear restores PMM to 0 after the probe, but no HFENCE.GVMA is issued between the set and clear, nor after the final clear. If the host CPU has residual G-stage TLB state from a previous guest, the transient PMM enable/disable could briefly create the aliasing condition. However, this runs during VCPU init before the guest actually executes, so the practical risk is low.
findings.snippet:
csr_set(CSR_HENVCFG, value);
return (csr_read_clear(CSR_HENVCFG, ENVCFG_PMM) & ENVCFG_PMM) == value;

findings.finding: henvcfg initialization correctly sets PBMTE, STCE, CBIE, CBCFE, CBZE, ADUE based on ISA extensions but explicitly does NOT set any PMM bits. PMM starts at PMLEN=0 (disabled), which is the safe default.

henvcfg is correctly written to hardware during vcpu_load via both NACL and direct CSR paths. This is the normal path for henvcfg updates. The issue is that the SBI FWFT handler bypasses this load/put cycle.

vcpu_put correctly saves guest CSRs but does not save/restore henvcfg, which is an HS-mode CSR written during vcpu_load. This is correct behavior — henvcfg does not need save/restore across vCPU switches since each vcpu_load overwrites it.
findings.snippet:
csr->vsstatus = csr_read(CSR_VSSTATUS);
// ... saves VS CSRs but not HENVCFG

findings.finding: The assembly switch routine correctly saves/restores GPRs and key CSRs (SSTATUS, STVEC, SEPC, SSCRATCH, HSTATUS). It does not touch henvcfg, which is handled separately in C code. No vulnerability here.
findings.snippet:
REG_S  ra, CTX_RA(t0)
// ... GPR and CSR save/restore
